summary: North Korea is essentially closed to tourism: borders shut in 2020 and have reopened only for limited, state-organized group tours aimed chiefly at the Russian market. Tourists normally travel only on organised tours whose state-approved operator arranges the visa, independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.

declarations.text: Foreign currency must be declared to customs on arrival, and foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border. GPS devices are held by customs until you leave. currencyLimits.text: There are no limits on bringing in or taking out foreign currency, but you must declare it at customs. Importing or exporting North Korean won (KPW) is illegal; shops and restaurants usually charge foreigners in foreign currency, and some hotels insist on full cash payment in advance.

notes: The UK government advises against bringing books or other written material in Korean, including anything religious, and says customs confiscate literature or media deemed anti-government, subversive or pornographic. Canada's travel advice says the same applies to material printed in South Korea.

The UK government says foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border and cannot connect to any network with an international SIM card, and GPS devices must be left with customs until you leave. Canada's travel advice says satellite phones and shortwave radios are confiscated on entry and usually returned on departure.

Ask your guide's permission before taking any photograph, the UK government advises; Canada's travel advice says photos or videos taken outside tourist areas can lead to confiscation of your equipment or detention.

payments.text: The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted; the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies, some places take Chinese yuan, and importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice adds that there are no ATMs, change in foreign currency is often unavailable, and some hotels accept credit cards with advance notice.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea. The risk of arbitrary arrest and long-term detention is real, consular assistance is minimal or non-existent, and visitors must follow state rules and their guides' instructions at all times.

tips.text: Most Western governments advise against all travel to North Korea, citing the serious risk of arbitrary arrest and long-term detention. US passports cannot be used for travel there at all under US law.

Never leave your guide, photograph without permission, or bring religious or South Korean material. Canada's travel advice says you must be accompanied by an official guide at all times and can be arrested for unsanctioned political or religious activity.
The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and only limited tourism has restarted; the position can change with little notice.

Expect to be offline: the UK government says a foreign mobile phone must be registered at the border and cannot connect to international or domestic networks with an international SIM card. Tell family and colleagues in advance.
Bring euros, US dollars or Chinese yuan in small denominations. Canada's travel advice says change in foreign currency is often unavailable.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for North Korea?
faq.answer: Yes — every visitor needs a visa, and it can only be arranged through a state-approved tour operator as part of an organized, guided tour. In practice tourism has been essentially closed since 2020, with only limited group tours (mainly for the Russian market) resuming. US and South Korean passport holders cannot visit at all.

faq.question: Can US citizens visit North Korea?
faq.answer: No. The restriction comes from the US side: since 2017 US law has declared US passports invalid for travel to, in or through North Korea unless specially validated by the State Department — validations are granted only in very narrow cases such as journalism or humanitarian work.

faq.question: Is North Korea open to tourists in 2026?
faq.answer: Barely. The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and that only limited tourism has restarted. Anyone considering a trip should check the current position with a specialist tour operator.

faq.question: Can I travel independently in North Korea?
faq.answer: Normally not. Tourists travel on organised tours with state-approved guides who accompany them at all times, so you cannot choose your own itinerary or wander unaccompanied. The UK Foreign Office notes that independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

faq.question: What money do tourists use in North Korea?
faq.answer: Cash only. The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan taken in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice adds that there are no ATMs.
